(1) in the case of resonant pumping in the graphene nanoribbon with the armchair edge the whole resonance line is pumped; (2) in the case resonant pumping in graphene nanribbons with the zigzag edge the whole resonance is divided into parts, each of them corresponds to the pumping one electron per cycle.
the pumped charge is proportional to the number of electrons in the pumping contour and that it can be positive or negative depending on the particular contour encircling the resonant line.

(i) for zigzag ribbons the pumped charge is determined by the part of the whole resonance line that is encircled by a pumping contour; (ii) the pumped charge can be positive or negative depending on the pumping contour; and (iii) for armchair ribbon the pumped charge is equal to one per cycle for any pumping contour.

the adiabatic quantum pumping in graphene nanobridge double barrier structures with zigzag and armchair edges.
the study of adiabatic quantum pumping in graphene nanoscale structures with zigzag and armchair edges.
the adiabatic charge pumping in graphene double barrier structures with zigzag and armchair edges in the resonating regime.

quantum charge pumping is a very efficient method to generate a current of electrons in graphene nanostructures.
the pumping in graphene nanribbons is more complex than in the case of carbon nanotubes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pumped charge is determined by the number of resonances in the pumping cycle.
in armchair ribbons one can pump one electron per cycle, while in zigzag ribbons one can do so in two different ways, pumping one electron per cycle in either direction.
for both armchair and zig-zag ribbons the pumped charge is a linear function of the pumping frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pumping current in graphene nanoribs is determined by the particular pumping contour and the edge geometry.
the resonant quantum charge pumping in the graphene nanostructures can be used to generate single electrons in a controlled manner.
in the resonant regime the pumped charge can be much greater than in the non-resonant regime.
